title: MAGIC ENGLISH GRADE 6 — WORLD 1: A2+ POWER-UP & B1 FOUNDATION
description: A high-volume transition world that moves learners from controlled A2 communication toward confident B1 English through vocabulary depth, grammar control, connected reading, natural listening, sustained speaking, practical writing and real-life problem solving.

targets.active_vocabulary: 850–950 words, collocations, phrasal verbs and functional expressions
targets.listening: 6–8 minutes, clear to natural multi-speaker English

progression.vocabulary: word → phrase → collocation → sentence → paragraph → conversation
progression.listening: slow clear speech → normal speed → natural connected speech
progression.speaking: guided answers → follow-up questions → role-play → independent discussion
progression.writing: controlled sentences → connected paragraph → structured short text

missions.title: Vocabulary Upgrade — Words That Work Together
missions.content: Build a powerful A2+ vocabulary system using learn/learning/learner, decide/decision, succeed/success/successful, improve/improvement and practical collocations such as make a decision, take responsibility and solve a problem.
missions.challenge: Use 20 target expressions in original sentences and a two-minute spoken summary.

missions.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Time Control
missions.challenge: Tell a personal-style fictional experience and explain exactly when specific events happened.

missions.title: Story Engine — Past Simple, Past Continuous & Past Perfect
missions.challenge: Rebuild a 250-word story from mixed events and then retell it without reading.

missions.title: Future Lab — Plans, Predictions & Instant Decisions
missions.challenge: Plan a three-day trip, predict problems and respond to unexpected changes.

missions.title: Modal Mission — Rules, Advice, Possibility & Permission
missions.challenge: Solve a school, travel and workplace situation using precise modal meaning.

missions.title: Conditional Gateway — Real Choices & Possible Futures
missions.challenge: Create and explain ten real-life if-sentences, then handle a problem-solving simulation.

missions.title: Sentence Builder — Relative Clauses & Better Details
missions.challenge: Turn 15 short sentences into clear, information-rich B1-style sentences.

missions.title: Connect Your Ideas — Because, Although, However & Therefore
missions.challenge: Build a coherent 200-word paragraph using at least 12 connectors correctly.

missions.title: People & Relationships — Communication Intelligence
missions.real_life: Ask for clarification, apologize, give advice, disagree politely and repair a misunderstanding.
missions.challenge: Complete a six-scene conversation where the relationship changes because of communication choices.

missions.title: B1 Conversation Lab — Eight-Minute Challenge
missions.conversation: Discuss school, hobbies, technology, travel, health and future plans; answer follow-up questions instead of giving isolated sentences.
missions.challenge: Maintain an eight-minute conversation with no translation and at least 15 connected responses.

missions.title: Reading Explorer — The Choice
missions.reading: 600–750-word narrative/informational text about a young person facing an important everyday decision.
missions.challenge: Identify evidence, infer two unstated ideas and summarize the text in 100 words.

missions.title: Listening Lab — Natural Conversations
missions.listening: 6–8-minute sequence with school, family, travel and service conversations moving from clear A2+ speech toward natural B1 speed.
missions.challenge: Complete a two-stage listen: first gist, then detailed evidence without replaying every sentence.

missions.title: Writing Lab — My Experience, My Lesson
missions.writing: Write 180–220 words about an experience, including what happened, what caused it, how the situation changed and what was learned.
missions.challenge: Use at least three past-time forms, eight connectors and ten target vocabulary items.

missions.title: Dialogue Builder — From Script to Spontaneous English
missions.real_life: Build dialogues for meeting someone new, changing a plan, asking for help and solving a misunderstanding.
missions.challenge: Complete the same dialogue three times: with prompts, with partial prompts and independently.

missions.title: Real-Life English — Travel Mission
missions.real_life: Handle a complete journey from station to hotel, including a missed connection, a booking problem and a request for help.
missions.challenge: Use polite questions, clarification phrases and alternative solutions under time pressure.

missions.title: Real-Life English — Health, Safety & Public Services
missions.real_life: Describe a problem clearly, answer questions, understand instructions and ask for appropriate help in a pharmacy, clinic or public service setting.
missions.challenge: Complete a multi-step role-play while distinguishing urgent information from background details.

missions.title: Opinion Lab — Explain Your Thinking
missions.challenge: Give a two-minute opinion, answer three challenges and reformulate one answer more clearly.

missions.title: Problem-Solving Simulation — One Day, Five Problems
missions.scenario: A learner has a transport delay, a missed appointment, a broken phone, a school/work deadline and a money problem on the same day.
missions.challenge: Choose priorities, explain decisions, request help and change the plan when new information appears.

missions.title: B1 Integrated Skills Marathon
missions.assessment: Vocabulary retrieval → grammar correction → 650-word reading → 7-minute listening → 5-minute speaking → 200-word writing.
missions.challenge: Complete the full sequence with limited translation and maintain meaning while working under time limits.

missions.title: WORLD 1 MASTER QUEST — A2+ TO B1 FOUNDATION
missions.final_quest: A cinematic integrated mission combining vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, reading, listening, speaking, conversation, writing and real-life problem solving.
missions.mastery_standard: Learner can understand the main points of clear natural English, communicate connected ideas, describe experiences, explain reasons, handle common real-life problems and produce independent A2+/early-B1 English.

assessment.vocabulary: retrieval, collocation matching, word-family formation, sentence production
assessment.grammar: meaning-focused selection, correction, transformation and production
assessment.reading: gist, detail, inference, reference, vocabulary in context
assessment.listening: gist, detail, speaker intention, sequence and note-taking
assessment.speaking: fluency, intelligibility, connected speech, interaction and task completion
assessment.writing: organization, grammar control, vocabulary range, connectors and clarity
assessment.real_life: successful completion of practical communication tasks

unlock.world_2: locked until World 1 mastery criteria are met
